record_contextual.why: Every quasi-identifier group holds at least k distinct subscribers, so no record can be isolated on the published attributes.
evidence: A1: 0.0% of rows unique, identification probability 0.025

record_simplified.why: An attacker who also knows the target's rough data volume pushes 2.01% of rows into groups smaller than k, so those individuals are identifiable with probability above 1/k.
evidence: A1: 0.0% of rows unique, identification probability 0.025
A4: 2.01% of rows below k when volume is known

aggregate_contextual.why: The aggregate release contains no records at all — the smallest published unit is a cell of at least k = 10 distinct subscribers — so there is nothing to isolate.
evidence: Every published cell clears k = 10 on the noisy count

aggregate_simplified.why: The aggregate release contains no records at all — the smallest published unit is a cell of at least k = 10 distinct subscribers — so there is nothing to isolate.
evidence: Every published cell clears k = 10 on the noisy count

record_contextual.why: The record release carries no subscriber key, hash or pseudonym, so two rows cannot be attributed to the same person.
evidence: A2: no key in the release

record_simplified.why: The record release carries no subscriber key, hash or pseudonym, so two rows cannot be attributed to the same person.
evidence: A2: no key in the release

aggregate_contextual.why: No records exist to link and the subscriber key was destroyed, not hashed. Linkage-shaped risk against this release is measured under No Inference (A5 differencing, A6 membership).
evidence: Structural: counts only, no key retained

aggregate_simplified.why: No records exist to link and the subscriber key was destroyed, not hashed. Linkage-shaped risk against this release is measured under No Inference (A5 differencing, A6 membership).
evidence: Structural: counts only, no key retained

record_contextual.why: No quasi-identifier group is homogeneous on the revealing value of any sensitive attribute.
evidence: A3: 0% of subscribers have an attribute disclosed

record_simplified.why: 94% of groups are homogeneous on the negative value — a far weaker disclosure, but still an inference.
evidence: A3: 0% of subscribers have an attribute disclosed

aggregate_contextual.why: Neither aggregate attack is attemptable by the defined recipient: differencing needs the true slice totals and membership inference needs every other subscriber's data.
evidence: A5 and A6: not attemptable contextually

aggregate_simplified.why: Membership inference reaches 54.0% against a 50% coin flip — a real edge, but inside the 73.1% the budget allows.

linkage_counterfactual.headline: if rows were linkable, 99.3% unique at 4 points
linkage_counterfactual.detail: That is the counterfactual we designed against, not a property of either release. Neither release keeps a subscriber key, so the attack has nothing to join on — which is exactly why the key was destroyed rather than hashed.
